chapter: Building the band, Ivie Anderson and touring
title: Hustle: plugging friends' businesses in ad-libs
summary: Greer adds current events and paid plugs to his stage patter.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I had friends that was in business, different business, the guys would come up and say, 'Sonny, give me a plug,' Okay, I would insert it. Yeah, liquor store, I don't care, anything. Hairdressers, anything, I would slide it in there, you know.

That was my inside hustle and just did it, you know, and I recall one time, we were playing the theatre, Loew's Theatre, Loew's, Academy of Music or something up in Brooklyn, and Milton Berle, Uncle Miltie, he was a big thing on television, so we are sitting up there, we're get the stage set. He used to always come running out at that time, always wanted -- he was Berle, so then he would do his act, so he passed by, and I say, 'Hey man, you better get all the laughs you can, because we're coming through.'

He look at me like I'm crazy. I said, 'Man, you better get the laughs, because they ain't going to be none left when we get through,' and sure enough we was (Unintelligible) because we kept it so that all the current events like, you see Bob Hope, we was doing that long before him, man. And we washed everybody away. I used to tell them guys, all them guys supposed to be funny, comedians, you better get all the laughs you can because
me and Ivie going to be coming through there. And we used to smother them. That's right, that's no exaggeration, that's the true fact.
